newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - May 10.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet:
biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
FEDERAL POLICE TO SEEK PERMISSION TO PROSECUTE YADAV

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) will officially seek the Bihar governor's sanction to prosecute Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav for involvement in a 9.5 billion rupee animal fodder scandal. The investigating agency was expected to submit a formal case report to the governor on Saturday. Although the CBI chief had cleared the proposal to seek the governor's sanction for the chief minister's prosecution on April 27, the agency took nearly 15 days to prepare what it considered a fool-proof case.
The Hindustan Times
BIHAR CHIEF MINISTER WILL SKIP PARTY PANEL MEET

Bihar Chief Minister Laloo Prasad Yadav has decided to skip the United Front Steering Committee's crucial meeting at which the situation arising out of the federal police decision to prosecute him was likely to be deliberated upon. Although the party said the issue was not on the Steering Committee's agenda, some of its top leaders hinted at the possibility of a discussion on this sensitive matter.
The Economic Times
MINISTER QUESTIONS DUTIES ON PETROLEUM SECTOR

The Petroleum Ministry has sent a fresh cabinet note elaborating the options before the government to tackle the petroleum product price problem. Besides hiking oil prices, the options include budgetary support, rolling back excise and import duties and partially passing the burden of subsidies to the Fertiliser Ministry. The minister of state for petroleum said oil companies could not continue operations beyond July if the oil pool deficit is not tackled.
PANEL ENDORSES PRIVATE SECTOR ENTRY INTO INSURANCE

The parliamentary standing committee on insurance sector reforms has broadly endorsed the Malhotra Committee recommendations to allow private sector entry into insurance, and called for a level playing field between the public and private sector. The committee said the LIC and the GIC Act should also be suitably amended to restore the original powers of the Controller to the Insurance Regulatory Authority. The panel report, which reflects a growing consensus among political parties to unshackle the sector, nevertheless clarified that no single company should be allowed to transact both life and general insurance business.
MARUTI RECALLS 50,000 DEFECTIVE CARS

Maruti Udyog (MUL) will recall 50,000 cars, manufactured between November 1996 and April this year, following the detection of component defects. The cost of such a recall would usually be borne by the car manufacturer, which, in turn, would retrieve it from the component manufacturer.
SOROS COMMITS FIVE BLN RUPEES FOR REFINERY

U.S.-based fund manager George Soros has committed five billion rupees as promoter's equity for a six million tonne grassroots refinery scheduled to come up in Haldia. The project would have a debt component of 18 billion rupees and equity of around 12 billion rupees. Soros had initiated discussions with leading financial institutions to tie up domestic debt.
Financial Express
FALL IN FOREIGN INSTITUTIONS' INVESTMENTS

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has permitted 15 new foreign financial institutions (FIIs) in the first four months of 1997, taking the total number of registered FIIs to 443. The list of new FIIs registered with the market regulator include Templeton Investment Counsel, The Yasuda Trust & Banking Company, Global Fund, Morgan Guarantee Trust, ABN Amro Investment and Fondigest Spa of Italy. But total investments by all the SEBI-registered FIIs is sharply lower at around $460 million against $1,500 million during the same period last year.
SCRAMBLE FOR BANK OF INDIA SHARES

The scramble for Bank of India (BOI) shares, buoyed by foreign and domestic institutional investors' purchases, pushed up the stock by 30 percent since its listing a week ago. The bank was yet to dispatch share certificates to over 200,000 investors, brokers said. BOI shares, offered at 45 rupees per share and listed on the Bombay Stock Exchange at 50.25 rupees, closed on Friday at 73.25 rupees. On the National Stock Exchange, the stock closed at 73.85 rupees, a jump of 15.56 percent over its listing price two days back.
Business Standard
CUT IN PSF PRODUCTION URGED

The Indian Fibre Manufacturers Association had invited polyester staple fibre (PSF) makers Reliance Industries and Indo Rama Synthetics to join the body in a desperate bid to check the slide in PSF prices. The association also requested the duo to reduce production by at least 20 percent. The association's president said Reliance and Indo Rama had forced PSF prices down, which made the operations of other manufacturers unviable. The two majors together produce about 33,000 tonnes of PSF annually, while the total demand for the product stands at 32,000 tonnes. The domestic aggregate installed PSF capacity is close to 45,000 tonnes per annum.
AMOCO SET FOR SECOND COMING, COMMITS $4 BLN TO LNG VENTURE

Amoco Corp, the U.S. energy and chemicals giant which pulled out of India last year, has committed itself to an investment of $4 billion for a facility to produce five million tonnes of liquefied natural gas (LNG) a day from Qatar's vast reserves, to be shipped to the Hazira power refineries and petrochemicals complex. Amoco would invest $650 million towards a regassificiation plant at Hazira. The LNG would be used for creating a power generation capacity of approximately 4,000 megawatts at Hazira. This demands an additional investment of $4 billion, in which, again, Amoco would be interested.
NEW REGISTRATION MANDATORY FOR EXISTING NBFCS

In a major tightening of norms for non-banking finance companies (NBFCs), the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has directed registered NBFCs to re-register before July 8. The new RBI Act stated that carrying on business without a certificate of registration was an offence punishable with imprisonment or fine. The NBFCs were also asked to create a reserve fund and transfer to it not less than 20 percent of the net profit every year. Appropriations from the fund would be controlled by the RBI. The RBI had also been given powers to commence winding up proceedings against defaulting NBFCs.
NATIONAL IRANIAN OIL TO HIKE STAKE IN MRL

The National Iranian Oil Company will hike its stake in Madras Refineries to 13 percent from 10 percent. The company did not subscribe to Madras Refineries' rights issue in 1994, owing to which its stake was reduced to 10 percent. The unsubscribed portion will be picked up by the Iranian oil company now. The company's equity base would thus remain undiluted, even as it would benefit from a capital inflow of about 450 million rupees. To keep pace with the opening up of the oil sector, Madras Refineries had appointed a restructuring committee to suggest ways to increase production and improve its financial prospects.
The Observer
FREE IMPORT OF MANY ELECTRONICS ITEMS ON CARDS

The government would allow free imports of several electronic and electrical items soon. The Department of Electronics (DOE) has sent a list of 30 items to the Commerce Ministry for its approval. DOE also prepared a list of items on which it would like quantitative restrictions to be reviewed. The move came in the wake of India signing the World Trade Organisation treaty for the removal of the quantitative restrictions on electronics and Information Technology products in a phased manner.
LOWER HOUSE PASSES FINANCE BILL

The lower house of parliament has passed the Finance Bill for 1997, which seeks to give effect to the tax proposals contained in the budget, completing the budgetary exercise for the current fiscal. The bill would now go before the upper house for being returned to the President for his assent before May 14. The bill was passed by a voice vote as the finance minister rejected opposition's amendments and ruled out any modifications in line with the suggestions made by the Congress and the Left parties. While the Bharatiya Janata Party withdrew some amendments, the Left parties did not press for them.
BILL SUGGESTS REGULATIONS IN BROADCAST SECTOR

Political parties and religious bodies would be barred from getting a licence to start a broadcasting channel if the present provisions of the Broadcasting Bill, which was passed by the cabinet, becomes law. The bill said even individual companies or groups of companies would be banned from operating a licence if any political party or its associates were participants in the company with more than 5 percent interest. Stringent norms were laid down for disqualification of political and religious parties before being given the final approval by the Union Cabinet.
BASIS FOR DEPB RATE SPELT OUT BY COMMERCE SECRETARY

The calculation of the rate on the Duty Entitlement Pass Book (DEPB) scheme would be based on the average weighted customs duty on the cost, insurance and freight value. This percentage calculated on the free on board value would give rise to the DEPB credit rate. This basis for calculation was announced by the commerce secretary, who said there had been a delay in coming up with the rates for individual industries on account of difference of opinions between the finance and commerce ministries.
